name: BAUXITE
summary: A Dragos-designated, state-aligned OT threat group linked by substantial technical overlap to the IRGC-affiliated CyberAv3ngers persona.
primaryFocus: Operational technology and industrial control systems

stateAffiliation.assessment: State-aligned; the strongest public attribution applies to the overlapping CyberAv3ngers activity rather than to the BAUXITE name in isolation.

observedSince.label: BAUXITE activity cluster
observedSince.qualification: Dragos lists BAUXITE activity as dating from 2017.

observedSince.label: CyberAv3ngers persona
observedSince.qualification: MITRE reports CyberAv3ngers as active since at least 2020.

designations.name: BAUXITE
designations.description: The primary name for the activity cluster described in this profile.

designations.name: CyberAv3ngers
designations.description: MITRE's group record for the persona whose activity substantially overlaps BAUXITE.

designations.name: IRGC-affiliated cyber actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona
designations.description: Government reporting attributes the Unitronics activity to IRGC-affiliated actors using the CyberAv3ngers persona.

designations.name: Soldiers of Solomon
designations.description: Reported as connected to CyberAv3ngers; not treated as an alias for BAUXITE.

assessment.text: BAUXITE is an OT-focused activity cluster capable of reaching Stage 2 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain. Public reporting describes PLC compromise, ladder-logic modification, internet-scale reconnaissance and custom Linux backdoor deployment against OT and IoT devices.

The public evidence supports a strong overlap with CyberAv3ngers, but vendor and government labels represent different analytic scopes. This profile therefore keeps BAUXITE, CyberAv3ngers, G1027 and IRGC-affiliated reporting visibly separated.

Observed operations favour exposed devices, default or absent credentials, publicly documented weaknesses and device-specific payloads. The resulting risk is disproportionate because modest access paths can produce loss of view, availability and operator control in physical processes.

technologies.name: Firewalls, routers, HMIs and embedded controllers

campaigns.name: Unitronics targeting waves
campaigns.summary: IRGC-affiliated actors accessed internet-facing Unitronics PLC/HMI devices that used default or no passwords, replaced ladder logic and defaced operator displays. CISA reports at least 75 affected U.S. devices, including at least 34 in water and wastewater.
campaigns.impact: Loss of view, loss of availability, operational interruption and the potential for deeper cyber-physical effects.

campaigns.name: OT reconnaissance and research
campaigns.summary: Dragos observed reconnaissance and research against OT/ICS entities and devices. No follow-on activity was observed publicly, but the collection was assessed as useful preparation for later disruptive operations.
campaigns.impact: Reduced preparation cost for later attempts to manipulate control and view or cause loss of availability.

campaigns.name: IOCONTROL deployment
campaigns.summary: A custom Linux backdoor was compiled for multiple OT and IoT device families and communicated with command infrastructure over MQTT on TCP 8883 after resolving its domain through DNS over HTTPS. Dragos reported approximately 400 confirmed victims.
campaigns.impact: Persistent remote command execution, port scanning, self-deletion and potential lateral movement from embedded devices. Dragos notes that the malware itself contains no ICS-specific functionality.

capabilities.name: Compromise exposed PLCs and modify ladder logic
capabilities.description: Public reporting documents authentication to exposed Unitronics devices, erasure of original ladder logic and download of actor-controlled logic.

capabilities.name: Exploit public knowledge and weak device security
capabilities.description: BAUXITE tracks OEM and protocol advisories, uses publicly known exploits and benefits from default credentials and exposed management services.

capabilities.name: Deploy tailored Linux backdoors
capabilities.description: IOCONTROL is a modular embedded-Linux backdoor with MQTT command and control, command execution, port scanning and persistence functions.

capabilities.name: Conduct internet-scale OT research
capabilities.description: The group researches exposed devices, OEM material and ICS protocol information to catalogue future opportunities.

malware.name: IOCONTROL
malware.description: A target-configurable backdoor for Linux-based OT and IoT devices. It uses encrypted MQTT communications, DNS over HTTPS for C2 resolution, daemon-based persistence and commands for execution, scanning and self-deletion.
malware.caveat: Dragos assesses that IOCONTROL has no ICS-specific functionality even though compromised devices can sit in or affect operational environments.

enterprise.name: Brute Force
enterprise.behaviour: CISA maps attempts against exposed Unitronics devices and their authentication paths to brute force activity.

enterprise.name: Valid Accounts: Default Accounts
enterprise.tactic: Initial Access / Persistence / Privilege Escalation / Defence Evasion
enterprise.behaviour: Actors authenticated to internet-connected PLC/HMI devices that retained default credentials or had no password configured.

enterprise.name: Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
enterprise.behaviour: The actors erased original ladder-logic files and downloaded replacement logic intended to disrupt operation and frustrate recovery.

ics.name: Internet Accessible Device
ics.behaviour: The Unitronics campaign reached PLC/HMI and supporting network devices directly exposed to the public internet.

ics.name: Insecure Credentials: Default Credentials
ics.behaviour: Affected devices used the Unitronics default password or no password, allowing remote authentication.

ics.name: Denial of Service
ics.behaviour: Controller defacement and logic changes prevented normal operation and contributed to communications failures.

ics.name: Loss of Availability
ics.behaviour: Compromised PLC/HMI devices became unavailable for normal business and operational use.

ics.name: Loss of Productivity and Revenue
ics.behaviour: Victims halted or constrained industrial activity while affected controllers were unavailable.

ics.name: Loss of View
ics.behaviour: Replacement HMI graphics prevented operators from viewing legitimate controller information.

defensivePriorities.title: Remove direct internet exposure
defensivePriorities.description: Place PLCs, HMIs and embedded management interfaces behind controlled remote-access paths and verify that default service ports are not publicly reachable.

defensivePriorities.title: Eliminate default and absent credentials
defensivePriorities.description: Set strong unique passwords, enable multifactor authentication where supported and inventory devices that cannot meet the control.

defensivePriorities.title: Monitor logic and configuration integrity
defensivePriorities.description: Alert on PLC program downloads, ladder-logic changes, HMI graphic replacement, port changes and disabled upload or download functions.

defensivePriorities.title: Hunt IOCONTROL behaviour, not only old indicators
defensivePriorities.description: Correlate embedded-Linux persistence, DNS over HTTPS, MQTT over TCP 8883, unexpected port scanning and remote command execution from OT-adjacent devices.

defensivePriorities.title: Segment and preserve operator visibility
defensivePriorities.description: Restrict conduits between IT, IoT and OT zones, retain independent engineering backups and ensure operators can recover trusted logic and display state.
